_meta.title: Session 34 — Leaderboard sweep: SubQ (Subquadratic) new model
_meta.context: Periodic reference-link + leaderboard sweep for new models since the Opus 4.8 ingest. Cross-checked llm-stats.com release feed, artificialanalysis.ai, and WhatLLM May-2026 roundup against DB. Result: nearly all May-2026 launches already tracked (Opus 4.8, Gemini 3.5 Flash, Qwen3.7 Max, Grok 4.3, GPT-5.5 Instant, ZAYA1-8B, Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite). ONE genuinely-new model: SubQ 1M-Preview (Subquadratic, Miami startup, emerged from stealth May 5 2026, $29M seed). First frontier-scale LLM on a fully sub-quadratic sparse attention (SSA) architecture instead of a transformer — native 12M-token context, near-linear compute/memory scaling, vendor claims ~52x faster attention at scale + ~1/5 frontier cost on long-context. Vendor-published benchmark scores: RULER@128K 95.0% (vs Opus 4.6 94.8% at ~325x lower cost: $8 vs ~$2,600), MRCR v2@1M 65.9%, SWE-Bench Verified 81.8%.
_meta.rule: STRICT-ATTRIBUTION with CAVEAT. SubQ scores are VENDOR-SELF-REPORTED (Subquadratic launch materials) — no peer-reviewed paper yet ('paper coming soon'), not independently reproduced, narrow eval scope. Each score has model+benchmark+value from the vendor as primary source, so admitted, but every note flags the unverified status. RULER 128K cited as 95.0 (some secondary sources say 97/97.1; 95.0 chosen as the value tied to the vendor's $8-vs-$2,600 cost comparison). Other May-2026 launches confirmed already in DB — no other new scored models found.

models.name: SubQ 1M-Preview
models._note: First frontier-scale LLM on a fully sub-quadratic sparse attention (SSA) architecture — content-dependent sparse routing computes exact attention only on relevant tokens, near-linear scaling. Native 12M-token context window. Miami startup, out of stealth May 5 2026 with $29M seed. Vendor claims ~52x faster attention at scale + ~1/5 frontier cost on long-context workloads. NO peer-reviewed paper yet (pending) — all scores vendor-self-reported, not independently reproduced.

benchmarks.name: RULER @ 128K
benchmarks.description: RULER long-context retrieval/reasoning benchmark at 128K context. Synthetic needle-in-haystack + multi-hop variable tracking + aggregation across a 128K window. Higher=better accuracy.
